text:
lina: quick sync: customer demand for strict geo-residency broke our active-active prefetch assumptions. proposing a small-surface change: signed read-leases + opt-in redirect fallback. thoughts?
mike: sketch: primary issues signed lease token (tenant, seq, expiry) on write. secondaries can serve cached responses only if they present valid lease. otherwise proxy redirects to resident region. no request/response payloads cross regions.
anya: that would avoid cross-region copies of inference artifacts. how do we revoke leases quickly if tenant flips residency?
julie: control-plane publishes revoke events to proxy pubsub; proxies hold lease TTL fallback 30s. revocation sets local_seq to INF so all tokens invalid.
legal-bot: checklist: token metadata (seq, ts) is OK, but tokens must not include request-derived hashes or content. Any payload-level replication is disallowed for strict-residency.
ops-bot: metrics to add: `geo.lease_issue_rate`, `geo.redirect_rate`, `geo.stale_served_rate`. alert if redirect_rate > 2% for non-strict tenants.
mike: edge: warm-up in secondaries — without cross-region prefetch, cold reads will redirect until local warm completes. consider `async-local-warm` that runs only in-region.
lina: action items: @mike implement token format + signing, @anya add control-plane revoke + pubsub, @julie update privacy runbook, @ops-bot schedule canary with 3 tenants. we'll review Monday. tl;dr: opt-in signed lease + redirect fallback keeps inferred data resident while allowing safe reads in warm cases.
